title: A novel, putatively null, FGD1 variant leading to Aarskog-Scott syndrome in a family from UAE

reviewer.method: Complete 215-line main-text reading, three whole figure pixel inspections, complete text-only Methods DOCX extraction/read and all items in both family packets compared.

audit.exposure_note: Prior aggregate compact-cohort performance and source-audit coverage were seen in the biology/laboratory task context. No per-case ranking output for this assigned review queue was consulted. This is an exposed post-inference audit, not blinded.

patient_identity.statement: Male IV-5 is the younger brother described at three years.

genotype.statement: Both brothers carry hemizygous FGD1 c.53del, predicted p.Pro18Argfs*106; their mother is heterozygous.

segregation.statement: Hemizygous affected sons and heterozygous mother support the reported X-linked segregation.
limitations: Other relatives with short stature/developmental findings are not molecularly established carriers; consanguinity is reported.

phase.statement: One hemizygous X-linked allele is represented; diploid cis/trans phase is inapplicable. No phase measurement is inferred.

causal_confidence.statement: Authors assign a putatively null frameshift as the cause of Aarskog-Scott syndrome based on sequence, predicted truncation and clinical concordance.
limitations: Protein loss/function was predicted, not assayed. Neurobehavioral and obesity attribution remains less specific than the core syndrome.

phenotype_completeness.statement: Packet selects features from the clinical descriptions and images; ophthalmic/ENT findings, detailed milestones, initial growth and later age context are not exhaustively represented.
limitations: No systematic negative-feature assessment is supplied; absent mention is not proof of absence.

assessment.statement: The source supports hemizygous c.53del and predicted p.Pro18Argfs*106. Methods explicitly use NM_004463.2, whereas the packet uses NM_004463.3 and additional GRCh38 genomic/VCF representations. Those conversions are not independently validated here.
limitations: Transcript-version and genomic normalization require a separate reference mapping; no mismatch is called a proven wrong allele.
